info.title: Lunar Landing Site Navigator API
info.description:
NASA Space Apps 2026 API for evaluating Lunar South Pole landing sites using LOLA DEM/slope/PSR datasets, 360-degree horizon raycasting, and SPICE ephemerides.

- **Swagger UI:** `/docs`
- **ReDoc:** `/redoc`
- **OpenAPI JSON:** `/openapi.json`
- **Health:** `/api/v1/health`

get.description:
Lunar elevation tile for the globe in the Moon Trek / Cesium geographic scheme (handoff P-008).

Covers the whole Moon so the globe can use a single terrain source: the LOLA south polar
DEM (20/40/80 m, best fit for the zoom level) where it has data, the global LOLA DEM elsewhere.
Level 10 (~21 m/px) reads the 20 m polar DEM.

parameters.name: z

schema.description: Zoom level (0 to 10). Level 0 has 2 columns x 1 row
schema.title: Z

parameters.description: Zoom level (0 to 10). Level 0 has 2 columns x 1 row

parameters.name: row

schema.description: Tile row, 0 = north edge (0 to 2^z - 1)
schema.title: Row

parameters.description: Tile row, 0 = north edge (0 to 2^z - 1)

parameters.name: col

schema.description: Tile column, 0 starts at -180 deg (0 to 2^(z+1) - 1)
schema.title: Col

parameters.description: Tile column, 0 starts at -180 deg (0 to 2^(z+1) - 1)

200.description: 256x256 Terrarium PNG (samples at pixel centers): elevation_m = R*256 + G + B/256 - 32768, relative to the 1,737,400 m lunar sphere. Headers: X-Terrain-Source names the DEM used; X-Terrain-Resolution-M is the spacing in metres of the DEM data actually read (native pixel times the decimation factor, the coarsest one when the tile mixes sources).

404.description: Requested resource or route not found

422.description: z, row, col or a parameter outside its range

503.description: The LOLA DEMs on the server do not cover the tile

304.description: Not modified (If-None-Match matches the tile ETag)

get.description:
Terrain mesh heights for the globe, ready for Cesium's heightmap terrain (contract v1.5).

Same tiling scheme and DEM sources as /terrain/tiles, but on a 65 x 65 vertex grid that
includes the tile edges: neighbouring tiles share bit-identical edge values, so the globe
passes the array to Cesium without resampling. Level 12 (~21 m between samples) reads the
20 m polar DEM.

parameters.name: z

schema.description: Zoom level (0 to 12). Level 0 has 2 columns x 1 row
schema.title: Z

parameters.description: Zoom level (0 to 12). Level 0 has 2 columns x 1 row

parameters.name: row

schema.description: Tile row, 0 = north edge (0 to 2^z - 1)
schema.title: Row

parameters.description: Tile row, 0 = north edge (0 to 2^z - 1)

parameters.name: col

schema.description: Tile column, 0 starts at -180 deg (0 to 2^(z+1) - 1)
schema.title: Col

parameters.description: Tile column, 0 starts at -180 deg (0 to 2^(z+1) - 1)

200.description: 65x65 little-endian float32 elevations in metres (16,900 bytes before gzip), row 0 = north edge, samples ON the tile edges and corners, quantized to 1/256 m. Relative to the 1,737,400 m lunar sphere. Sent with Content-Encoding: gzip when the client accepts it. Headers: X-Terrain-Source names the DEM used; X-Terrain-Resolution-M is the spacing in metres of the DEM data actually read (native pixel times the decimation factor, the coarsest one when the tile mixes sources).

get.description:
Relief shading of the whole Moon, ready to paint as an imagery layer (contract v1.5).

Lambert shading with a fixed, illustrative light: the light comes from the direction of
(light_lat, light_lon) in the Moon body-fixed frame (defaults: the globe's light). Slopes
are central differences on the DEM's own grid (polar stereographic with its scale factor,
or latitude/longitude), read from the raster around each pixel, so tiles have no seams.
Parameters are rounded to 0.01 for caching.
